chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn 'Alī, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the magician, and he said: 'If two just men come and testify against him, then his blood is lawful (to be killed).'

key_terms.حَلَّ دَمُهُ: His blood is lawful (to be killed/executed)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for killing a magician according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary standard for executing a magician, requiring the testimony of two just ('adl) witnesses, a criterion consistent with general Islamic legal principles for capital punishment. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the reliability and justice of witnesses in establishing the legality of shedding blood, distinguishing it from mere suspicion or single testimony.
